title: Answer review 2 in the squash-chain landing design
summary: As the user directed, this job only answers review 2 in the squash-chain design: it adds a response appendix for the six findings and revises §4.1, §4.6 and §5 to match. It also updates D69 and the changelog. Nothing is built; the build is a later job.

defaults_applied.how: The design is revised with alternatives and a response appendix before any build.
Each answer cites the review finding and the code it was checked against.
Design-only change; the build is split into a later job.
The appendix is written for an outside reader.

assumptions: Per the user's reply, this job only answers review 2 in the design; the build is a separate later job, so no Rust code, schema, or tests change.
previous_job is assumed derived by the core as the latest landed job in the base commit's history (absent if none); the design states this as a changeable assumption.
D69 stays proposed because the chain rule is not yet built.
Line rewrapping (R2-n2) is applied to the cited decisions.md and v0 design lines only if small.

acceptance_criteria.text: docs/design/squash-chain-landing.md gains an Appendix B answering each review-2 finding (R2-M1, R2-m1, R2-m2, R2-m3, R2-n1, R2-n2) with a disposition and the section changed; the review file is unchanged.

§4.1 defines how the core derives previous_job from the base commit (including after a hand change, a records-only commit, and an unlanded predecessor), states it as an assumption the user may change, and says what is written when none is found.

The design resolves R2-m2: one remaining job is judged by the single-job rule (or the head rule is extended, one stated), how a landed predecessor is found at P is specified, and a /1 predecessor is accepted or refused explicitly; §4.6 is made consistent.

The design resolves R2-m1 (merge-commit refusal message: either note that the existing merge message is shown or list a change to check that passes landing's reason through, with a test) and notes rules changes in R2-n1.
§5 items 1 and 2 name AnyRecord, the schema-name table, the consumers (athena-core run.rs, store.rs, athena-gate jobs.rs), and put RecordSet::load in athena-gate.
D69 in docs/decisions.md and the CHANGELOG entry are updated to reflect the answers; D69 stays proposed and no code or tests change; the build is left as a separate later job.
Run `cargo test` and `cargo fmt --check`: both pass (the repository's wording scan covers the docs).

out_of_scope: Building the chain rule: athena.candidate/2, core writes, gate landing rule, jobs::check and history changes, and code tests (a later job).
departures: Design-only docs change, slightly cheaper than the code-heavy history; otherwise the reference stands.
